collages.analysis:
1. CAMERA TECHNIQUES: The library includes wide-angle 24mm-35mm for environmental full-body shots with slight perspective distortion, and 85mm-135mm telephoto for compressed waist-up portraits. Apertures range from f/1.8 for shallow-depth-of-field separation to f/11 for sharp architectural detail. Angles vary from low-axis (2-foot height) to emphasize stature, to standard eye-level for clean catalog aesthetic.

2. FRAMING & COMPOSITION: Framing options range from expansive full-body shots with 40% negative space to tight editorial crops focusing on the torso. Layouts include centered symmetry for studio looks and rule-of-thirds offsets for environmental shots. Vertical 4:5 and 9:16 orientations dominate, often utilizing leading lines from background architecture.

3. LIGHTING RECIPES: Setups include hard, high-contrast direct sunlight creating 90-degree shadows; soft, diffused 5600K overcast light for even skin tones; and single-source studio lighting with rapid falloff. Backlighting at golden hour provides a 1-2 stop rim-light effect, while dappled shadows create geometric textures on subjects.

4. COLOR GRADE / PRESET CHARACTER: Palettes range from warm, sun-drenched ambers and terracotta to cool, desaturated neutrals. Contrast curves vary from lifted blacks for a matte film look to high-gamma punch. Film-stock emulation includes fine-grain textures, subtle 35mm noise, and organic highlight roll-off with a slight warm-balance bias.

5. SET & ENVIRONMENT FAMILIES: Environments comprise minimalist seamless studio sweeps, sun-bleached masonry walls, coastal horizons, and lush botanical textures. Locations are categorized by texture: rough stone, smooth plaster, reflective water, and organic foliage.

6. POSING & DIRECTION: Posing spans high-tension statuesque stillness to fluid, mid-stride motion. Direction includes weight-shifting for dynamic silhouettes, relaxed limb placement, and gaze ranges from 100% direct lens contact to 45-degree averted, pensive looks.

7. RETOCH & FINISH: Finishing focuses on naturalistic skin rendering with preserved pore detail and high micro-contrast in fabric textures. Highlights are recovered to maintain detail, while shadow depth is preserved to ensure a premium, non-digitized tactile quality.

1. CAMERA TECHNIQUES: Focal lengths range from 24mm wide-angle for environmental context to 85mm or 105mm primes for compressed editorial portraits. Apertures vary from f/1.8 for shallow depth-of-field to f/8.0 for total frame sharpness. Angles include 15-degree low-angle shots for stature and 0-degree eye-level shots for direct engagement.

2. FRAMING AND COMPOSITION: Framing strategies include full-body wide shots, 3/4 crops, and tight waist-up compositions. Subject placement utilizes both 50/50 centered symmetry and rule-of-thirds with 30-40 percent negative space. Composition often uses geometric architectural lines to lead the eye toward the subject.

3. LIGHTING RECIPES: Techniques include high-contrast direct sunlight with 4:1 ratios, soft-diffused overcast light, and 45-degree side-window lighting. Studio setups feature single-source key lights with deep shadow falloff or high-key seamless lighting. Backlighting is frequently used for 1-stop overexposed rim separation.

4. COLOR GRADE AND PRESET CHARACTER: Palettes vary from warm, high-saturation golden tones (6000K bias) to desaturated, cool-toned editorial neutrals. Contrast curves range from deep, crushed blacks to lifted shadows with a matte film-stock finish. Grain profiles mimic 35mm ISO 400 texture.

5. SET AND ENVIRONMENT FAMILIES: Repertoire includes minimalist studio seamless, geometric urban exteriors, sun-bleached natural landscapes, and sophisticated architectural interiors. Environments provide tonal contrast or monochromatic harmony to the subject.

6. POSING AND DIRECTION: Direction includes dynamic movement like mid-stride walking, relaxed asymmetrical weight distribution, and static sculptural poses. Gaze direction alternates between direct lens contact and ethereal off-camera focal points to vary the mood from assertive to candid.

7. RETOUCH AND FINISH: Skin rendering preserves natural pore texture with subtle frequency separation. Highlight roll-off is calibrated for a soft, analog feel. Micro-contrast is enhanced by 10-15 percent to define textures while maintaining a 5 percent sharpening threshold for a professional finish.
